turn.context: The version of record for part 3 (turn 24 was superseded). Six teams on the same footing, the reporting shape drawn: Head of Operations signs off, two managers as peers.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 27 · Part 3: Key people, rebuilt for both sides

text: Six teams touch this, plus two managers and one person who signs it off.
bullets: Nobody’s job changes. What changes is when they confirm something the system has already worked out.
The resistance sits in one place. It is being asked to name a discharge date a day early. Show the doctor a date to check, and it holds.
Both managers report to the Head of Operations. It is the only level that can tell both sides to work to one plan.
chat.pointer: Pick a team to see what changes for them.
chat.invite: Shall we move on to part 4, the teams and the numbers?
chat.note: Ask a doctor to check a date, not to produce one.
prompts: Yes, let us move on to part 4
What if the doctors still refuse?
Why not have one manager report to the other?

managers.title: Discharge Manager

blocks.tree_note: Same level, same size. Neither reports to the other.

sheets.title: Speak on the round
sheets.text: A spoken note on the round they already do. The system shows a predicted discharge date. The doctor confirms or corrects it with a tap.
sheets.entry: Which doctors would you ask first?

sheets.title: One round at 5 PM
sheets.text: One fixed round, only for beds expected to free tomorrow. They confirm or correct by 5 PM, so the plan freezes at 6 PM.

sheets.title: Told when to call
sheets.text: The desk stops guessing. It is told when to call each patient in, bed by bed.

lines.label: What changes
lines.value: Fewer calls, made at the right time

sheets.entry: Who runs your admissions desk today?

sheets.title: A release deadline per bed
sheets.text: The discharge team gets a deadline for each bed it is releasing, instead of a surprise in the afternoon.

lines.label: What changes
lines.value: A deadline they can plan to

sheets.entry: Who leads your discharge team today?

sheets.title: One new report
sheets.text: Bill close and bill open, read against the same bed. Both facts already exist in your system.

sheets.title: Read access, once
sheets.text: Your IT team gives read access to the systems you already run. After that, nothing more is asked.

lines.label: What changes
lines.value: One piece of work at the start

sheets.entry: Who in IT would we work with?

items.label: Where the resistance sits
items.sub: Naming a discharge date a day ahead is a clinical call. Checking a predicted date is not.

ask.label: Ask about this
ask.say: What if the doctors still refuse?

items.label: Extra clinical time
items.sub: This claim is wrong if the round gets longer to give the date. We would measure that from the first week.
